notes: the shape a consumer writes ($within against an external region) runs 38.89x faster over a derive: 'bbox' index than as a full scan — the two-stage plan is the whole difference
the in-memory engine over the parsed array is the row the database has to beat: it starts from objects where the store starts from bytes on a page, and the indexed store is 15.37x faster than it

the UDF hatch for $within: 0.86x as a sole predicate over a full scan, 9.01x beside a selective indexed conjunct, 39.96x with LIMIT 10 (> 1 is a push win; the residual comparator pushes everything but the spatial conjunct)

an R*Tree probe is 6.16x the generated-box B-tree on the same rows and box (> 1 favours the R*Tree); the R*Tree is a second table kept in sync transactionally and absent on any build without the module

no head-to-head rival: nothing else in JavaScript stores GeoJSON in SQLite from a JSON query document. MongoDB (2dsphere) and DuckDB-wasm (spatial) have real spatial indexes and overlay operations this suite does not; neither runs one document through three executors proven to agree
